title: RoutePlacer: An End-to-End Routability-Aware Placer with Graph Neural Network

problem.claim: Modern chip placement must account for routability, but current routability-oriented placers use an iterative two-stage process with non-differentiable routing feedback.

gap.claim: The two-stage approach prevents joint optimization of routability during placement.

contributions.claim: RoutePlacer is an end-to-end routability-aware placement method.
RouteGNN predicts routability by fusing geometric and topological placement representations.
RouteGNN provides a differentiable routability approximation for gradient-based optimization and can replace external routers in two-stage placers.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On DREAMPlace, RoutePlacer reduced Total Overflow by up to 16% while maintaining routed wirelength compared with the state-of-the-art.
Integrating RouteGNN into two-stage placers reduced Total Overflow by 44% without compromising wirelength.

narrative_sequence.summary: Placement quality depends critically on routability.
Existing two-stage routability-oriented placement hinders joint routability optimization.
RoutePlacer uses RouteGNN to predict routability and enable differentiable end-to-end optimization.
RouteGNN can also serve as a plug-and-play alternative to external routers in two-stage placers.
Experiments report reductions in Total Overflow while maintaining wirelength.

unknowns: Training data, model architecture details, and optimization procedure are unspecified.
Benchmarks, baselines, statistical variation, and evaluation conditions beyond DREAMPlace are unspecified.
